extracted.intended_audience: Prospective and current students of Magnet Theater improv, musical improv, sketch writing, and storytelling classes
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and expectations for participating in Magnet Theater's improv, musical improv, sketch writing, storytelling, and elective classes, including learning goals, progression/prerequisites, performance pathways, and registration/attendance/payment policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active, experiential learning
rubrics_metrics.description: All of our classes are active - you'll be on your feet, learning by doing, in a culture of mutual support and playful risk taking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The curriculum is designed to make students successful immediately and then build quickly on those successes in a strategic and focused way. Classes emphasize practice, participation, and learning through doing rather than passive lecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progressive curriculum and increasing sophistication
rubrics_metrics.description: Progressing through the levels will increase the sophistication of your work by integrating multiple aspects of scenework, group support, comedy technique and game playing, and longer improv structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is structured so each level builds on the previous; students must satisfactorily complete each level as a pre-requisite for the next level. Conservatory/upper levels require application acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced Improv program: performance focus and individualized attention
rubrics_metrics.description: The Advanced Improv Program provides advanced training, turning qualified students into consistent performers; it is performance focused, offering more individualized attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advanced classes include Advanced Improv 1, Advanced Level 2, Advanced Electives and Team Performance Workshop. The program is appropriate for veteran improvisers seeking to sharpen skills and for those preparing for consistent performance work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Musical Improv learning goals
rubrics_metrics.description: These classes teach students to sing confidently within their own voice, learn the mechanics of a song and the underlying structures songwriters use, and practice creating spontaneous musicals without pre-planned content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students practice repeatedly with a supportive group; after training, students may be asked to audition for Musical Megawatt teams and gain a regular performance slot. Magnet combines classroom instruction with growing performance opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sketch Writing learning goals and workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Sketch Writing classes teach the mechanics behind what makes great sketches work and apply that learning to each student's writing from concept to final polish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classes are structured like a 'writer's room' led by experienced instructors; students receive feedback and learn to analyze their own work to prepare for professional environments. Students build a writing packet; advanced classes culminate in performances cast from Magnet performers; opportunities to stage sketches include Sketch Club, The Generator, and Sketch Teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Storytelling learning goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Storytelling classes teach how to take personal experiences and create stories that an audience will deeply connect with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students learn the basic elements of narrative storytelling: how to surprise an audience, make them care, be real and truthful on stage, and discover and communicate the real meaning behind an experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electives purpose and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Elective classes augment the core curriculum by allowing students to build new specific skills, go deeper into areas they love, experiment, and work with different instructors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electives are shorter-term workshops (one-day or multi-week) that provide focused training and opportunities for exploration; offerings are added regularly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student expectations: punctuality and full participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Students are required to be on time to class and stay for the entire class period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be courteous to classmates. Disturbances such as tardiness, cell phone use, inappropriate comments, and disrespectful behavior will not be tolerated. Disruptive students may be asked to leave. If special accommodations are required, contact the School Director at registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance policy: maximum two absences
rubrics_metrics.description: Students may miss no more than 2 classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a student misses more than 2 classes, they may not be permitted to participate in the class show and must retake the class to move to the next level. An instructor may hold back a student and require them to repeat a class at their discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisites and placement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Students enter the program at Level 1 and must satisfactorily complete each level as a pre-requisite for the next level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conservatory (upper levels) requires acceptance through an application process. There is no pre-requisite for Drop-In, Free Intros, Any Level 1, Camp Magnet, or electives unless specifically noted. Magnet reserves the right to accept or deny an individual's registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance opportunities are not guaranteed
rubrics_metrics.description: Completion of the core curriculum and conservatory programs does not guarantee placement on a house team or guarantee any other performance opportunities at Magnet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should not assume automatic placement; performance slots and team membership are subject to separate selection/audition processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment policy: all sales final
rubrics_metrics.description: Class payments are non-refundable and non-exchangeable. All sales are final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students should be certain before paying; registration is not complete until payment is received in full.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration confirmation upon full payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration is not complete and you are not placed in the class until payment is received in full.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To secure a spot in a class you must complete payment; partial payment does not reserve placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescheduling and cancellation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If Magnet must cancel or reschedule a class, enrolled students will be notified by email or phone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the event of a cancelled class, students can choose to have a credit toward another class of the same financial value or receive a full refund. Rescheduling is rare but students will be notified.
